name: What is the best order of work for a primary bathroom remodel?

mainEntity.name: In what sequence should a primary bathroom remodel happen so the project stays on schedule?
mainEntity.text: In what sequence should a primary bathroom remodel happen so the project stays on schedule?

acceptedAnswer.text: A primary bathroom remodel should follow a logical sequence so the work does not get damaged or redone later. The usual order starts with design, measurements, product selections, and permits. After demolition, the contractor completes rough plumbing, electrical, framing changes, and ventilation work. Once those items pass inspection, waterproofing and tile work begin. Cabinetry, countertops, paint, trim, fixtures, mirrors, and glass come later, after the wet-area surfaces are complete. Final plumbing trim, lighting, and accessories are typically installed near the end, followed by punch-list corrections and final inspection. The sequence matters because waterproofing and inspections need to happen before finishes are covered. Homeowners should ask each contractor how they handle scheduling, inspections, and lead-time items so the project does not stall waiting for one missing product.
acceptedAnswer.description: The usual order is design and selections, permitting, demolition, rough plumbing and electrical, inspections, waterproofing, tile, cabinetry, countertops, paint, fixtures, glass, and final inspection. Following the correct sequence prevents rework and keeps waterproofing and finish details from being damaged later.
